_comments: Sales Contacts has DisplayNameAndEmail as its name field, deliberately and load-bearing:
.sales-contact-picker-columns.json turns on golive#259 around it ('the picker's name field is
DisplayNameAndEmail'), and the column plan is built by SUBTRACTING the name field, so which field
carries the flag decides both what the picker searches and which columns it renders.
THE FLAG THIS FILE CLEARS IS FirstName'S, and the reason is structural rather than a one-off.
CodeGen picks ONE name field per entity and clears every other flagged field, but it clears only
fields with AutoUpdateIsNameField = 1 -- a PINNED field is deliberately never touched in either
direction (MJ CodeGenLib manage-metadata.ts, applyNameFieldUpdates). DisplayNameAndEmail is
pinned AND ineligible to win: isFieldEligibleForNameField rejects any IsVirtual field that is not
an inherited IS-A column, and DisplayNameAndEmail is a sales-only concat defined in
vwSalesContactsGenerated -- it is not a column on Person, so it is virtual WITHOUT being
inherited. With no eligible flagged field, the reconciler falls through to its AI-ranked
candidates and picks FirstName (an inherited Person column, hence eligible), sets IsNameField on
it, and cannot clear the pinned one. Two fields end up flagged, against that method's own
documented 'single winner, always', and the view generator takes the lower Sequence: FirstName at
12 beats DisplayNameAndEmail at 34.
WHAT THAT COSTS, measured rather than feared: every denormalized contact-name column in the schema
is regenerated to join FirstName instead -- SalesContact on Deal Contact Roles, PrimaryContact and
BillingContact on Deals, DefaultPrimaryContact and DefaultBillingContact on Sales Accounts -- so
nvarchar(753) becomes nvarchar(100) and every deal and account surface shows a bare first name.
It also inverts golive#259 exactly: FirstName becomes the excluded name field while
DisplayNameAndEmail starts rendering as an ordinary column, which is the duplicate-looking-rows
complaint that issue exists to answer.
CLEARING BOTH FLAGS IS THE POINT. IsNameField alone would be re-set on the next pass, because
AutoUpdateIsNameField = 1 is what makes FirstName an auto-pick candidate at all. With both at 0
the eligible-candidate set no longer contains it, so the pinned field stays the only one flagged.
The window is narrow but real: the reconciler only re-evaluates on a pass that ADDS fields to the
entity, which is why this surfaced when the two inherited Person columns arrived and not before.
A host installing from migrations takes the fields from captured SQL and never runs it.
Nothing in the suite asserts on a contact's rendered name, so this regenerates green. It was found
by reading a @MaxLength(753) -> @MaxLength(100) change in the generated GraphQL schema.
